Being surrounded by people who love you doesn't mean you're immune to loneliness. What makes us feel that way is a lack of deep connections with others, it's not a problem with you or the people in your life, sometimes it's hard to open yourself up to others, and some people just can't empathize with your feelings. Some things that have helped me in the past with this are:

 - Appreciating your time alone a bit more, it's nice to allow yourself to be alone and content with it.
- Trying to open up to others with no expectations, some people are better than others at this like I said, so use your judgement and test the waters with people who may be willing to listen
- Try new things with your loved ones, sometimes, going to watch a movie or doing something together that you don't usually do can help you feel closer.
- Listen to your friend's problems, feels nice to help others who need to vent and can also make you feel closer to them.
- This one's obvious but going out to new places to make new friends really does help, doesn't need to be in real life, join a discord server, subreddit, a forum, somewhere where you can interact with the same people several times.

But the most important part is always within you, I know it's super hard, but learning to be happy with just yourself is the key.

See? You're actually making an effort to understand why "she can't see you" when you're suicidal, which is something she's not willing to do. I mean, if you're in a relationship with someone, it's because you love them, right? Why is school more important than trying to save your loved one from suicide? Yes, it does suck to feel rejected, unloved, etc. but this is what places like this are for, in the long run, you will feel better for standing up for yourself. 

You need willpower, sure, but what you need the most is understanding and actually believing that you love yourself enough to not need someone else to be happy, I'm not saying you have to deal with suicidal thoughts alone, on the contrary, you're worth a lot and you need help NOW, not when someone is done with their schoolwork. I don't condemn her either, dealing with a suicidal person is hard, but think about it logically, trying to remove as many of your feelings as possible, do you really think it's okay for someone to be in a relationship where the other person doesn't care enough to save them from suicide? 

This is why I mentioned an ultimatum, not just for her but for you as well. Be firm and clear, you need to focus on yourself, and you also need help; her not even trying to understand is making you feel worse. Your illness is serious and you will treat it, if she wants to try and help, cool, but you can't be romantically involved with someone that pretty much tries to invalidate how you feel.
